_comment: Chem WS2 — DERIVED. Chemical Reactions and Equations WS2 Class 10; no printed answer key; every answer derived. Q55 excluded (figure-dependent apparatus diagram).

1.reason: 2KClO3 heated with catalyst decomposes to KCl + O2; decomposition reaction and endothermic (requires continuous heat).

2.reason: a, c, d are all double displacement reactions; b (CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2) is a combination reaction, so it is the odd one out.

3.reason: REVIEW: 4NH3 + 5O2 -> 4NO + 6H2O is a redox reaction (iii true); it is conventionally also treated as a combination reaction in the keyed answer (ii). (i) displacement and (iv) neutralisation are false. Strictly only (iii) is correct, but the only paired option containing (iii) without a false partner is A (ii and iii).

4.reason: Rust is hydrated ferric oxide, Fe2O3.xH2O.

5.reason: NaHCO3 + HCl gives CO2, which turns lime water milky.

6.reason: Zn + H2SO4 -> ZnSO4(aq) + H2(g): ZnSO4 is aqueous and H2 is a gas, i.e. option (b).

7.reason: (iv) Zn + dilute H2SO4 is a displacement (not double displacement) and (v) acid + base is double displacement / neutralisation (not single displacement); both are incorrect matches.

8.reason: Slaked lime is calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2.

9.reason: The green coating (patina) on copper in moist air is basic copper carbonate.

10.reason: Crystallisation is a physical change; the identity of the substance is unchanged. Curdling, fermentation and digestion are chemical changes.

11.reason: REVIEW: Statement (i) is incorrect (the beaker becomes hot because the reaction is exothermic, not endothermic). The keyed answer is statement (i) only; statement (ii) 'clear solution' is debatable (Ca(OH)2 is sparingly soluble, often a milky suspension), but no option pairs (i) and (ii), and (iii) is correct, so A is the intended choice.

13.reason: Ferrous sulphate crystals (FeSO4.7H2O) are light/pale green.

14.reason: When an element burns in air it combines with oxygen; oxygen gains electrons and is reduced.

15.reason: Zinc granules have no regular shape, are silvery grey, and develop a brownish-black coating (deposited copper); all three observations are correct.

16.reason: BaCl2 + Na2SO4 -> BaSO4 (insoluble white ppt) + 2NaCl; it is both a double displacement and a precipitation reaction.

17.reason: Oils are stored under unreactive gases to prevent oxidation/rancidity; helium or nitrogen are suitable (oxygen would cause rancidity).

18.reason: 2NaOH + H2SO4 -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O is a neutralisation with no change in oxidation states, so it is not a redox reaction.

19.reason: Iron displaces copper from CuSO4; the solution turns pale green due to FeSO4 formation.

20.reason: Combustion of LPG is a chemical change; dissolution of salt, boiling of water and melting of ice are physical changes.

21.reason: Gold is a noble metal and does not corrode in moist air.

23.reason: A metal ribbon burning with a dazzling white flame to a white ash is magnesium: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO, a combination reaction (X = Mg, Y = MgO).

24.reason: REVIEW: Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu is a displacement reaction (the most specific classification). It is also a redox reaction (option A), but displacement is the intended answer.

25.reason: A reaction in which one element/radical is removed (displaced) by another is a displacement reaction.

26.reason: Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost releases heat, so it is exothermic.

27.reason: On thermal decomposition FeSO4 leaves a reddish/brownish-black residue of Fe2O3; of the options, brownish black is closest.

28.reason: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 is exothermic and forms a basic solution (pH more than 7).

29.reason: Zn + 2CH3COOH -> (CH3COO)2Zn + H2: zinc displaces hydrogen, a displacement reaction.

30.reason: Zinc is more reactive than copper and displaces it, decolourising the blue CuSO4 solution.

31.reason: 2AgCl --sunlight--> 2Ag + Cl2: silver metal and chlorine gas are formed (photochemical decomposition).

32.reason: A soluble lead salt is needed; lead acetate is soluble and can replace lead nitrate. Lead sulphate is insoluble.

33.reason: Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu: iron displaces copper, a displacement reaction.

34.reason: Ferrous sulphate solution is pale green (Fe2+ ions).

35.reason: Representing a reaction with formulae of reactants and products is a chemical equation.

36.reason: Balanced reaction: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + Heat (no H2 or O2 is released).

38.reason: Balancing a chemical equation follows the law of conservation of mass.

39.reason: BaCl2 + Na2SO4 -> BaSO4 (white ppt) + 2NaCl; barium chloride with sodium sulphate gives a white precipitate.

40.reason: Light green crystals that lose water and release SO2/SO3 (suffocating, blue litmus red) leaving reddish-brown residue are FeSO4.7H2O -> Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3.

41.reason: Al2O3 + 6HCl -> 2AlCl3 + 3H2O, so a = 1, b = 6, c = 2, d = 3.

42.reason: Chip packets are flushed with nitrogen, an inert gas, to prevent oxidation/rancidity.

43.reason: New products form only when the added metal is more reactive: (2) CuSO4 + Ca (Ca > Cu) and (4) ZnSO4 + Mg (Mg > Zn). So (b) and (d).

44.reason: Statement 1 is true (H2 + Cl2 --sunlight--> 2HCl), but Statement 2 is false: it is a combination reaction, not a displacement reaction.

45.reason: On heating FeSO4 the solid product is reddish-brown Fe2O3.

46.reason: Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2 is a redox reaction but not a combination reaction (A, B, D are all combination reactions).

47.reason: Fe + 2HCl -> FeCl2 + H2: hydrogen gas and iron(II) chloride are produced.

48.reason: Only statement (iii) is true. (i) is wrong (oxidation, not reduction, causes rancidity) and (ii) is wrong (bags are flushed with nitrogen, not oxygen).

49.reason: CuSO4 + H2S -> CuS (black ppt) + H2SO4 is a double displacement reaction.

50.reason: Heating FeSO4 crystals gives Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3 + H2O.

51.reason: The metal deposited on the iron nail is copper, which is reddish-brown.

52.reason: Evaporation of water is a physical change.

53.reason: Black-and-white photography uses the photochemical decomposition of silver salts (AgBr/AgCl).

54.reason: The pale green colour is due to FeSO4 formed when iron displaces copper from CuSO4.

56.reason: Copper is more reactive than silver and displaces it from AgNO3 solution; it cannot displace Ni, Zn or Fe (all more reactive).

57.reason: CH4 + Cl2 --sunlight--> CH3Cl + HCl is a substitution reaction.

59.reason: 2Pb(NO3)2 -> 2PbO + 4NO2 + O2: NO2, PbO and O2 are formed.

60.reason: A yellow precipitate forms when lead nitrate and potassium iodide solutions are mixed: Pb(NO3)2 + 2KI -> PbI2 (yellow) + 2KNO3.

61.reason: Aluminium displaces iron from Fe2O3 (thermite reaction), a displacement reaction.

62.reason: Sodium is oxidised (loses electrons) and therefore is the reducing agent.

63.reason: Slaked lime is the commercial name of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2.

64.reason: In Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2, CO is oxidised (to CO2) and Fe2O3 is reduced (to Fe). Oxidised then reduced = CO, Fe2O3.

65.reason: The colourless gas with a burning-sulphur smell that turns lime water milky and acidified K2Cr2O7 green is SO2.

55.reason: Beaker I (K2SO4) and II (NH4NO3) dissolving in water are endothermic, so their temperature falls. Beaker III (anhydrous CuSO4 + water -> hydration) and beaker IV (CuSO4 + Zn displacement/redox) are both exothermic, so their temperature rises. Only option D matches: temperature of III and IV rises while I and II fall.

58.reason: Experiment II curve is steeper and plateaus sooner (faster reaction -> a correct), both curves reach the same final CO2 volume (same amount of CaCO3 and HCl -> b correct), and a faster reaction at the same conditions means smaller chips with more surface area (c correct). Since statements a, b and c are all correct, the incorrect-statement answer is D, None of these.
